learningObjective: Compute the approximate weight-loading bandwidth saving of W4A16 vs FP16 for LLM decode.
profileData:
Model: 7B-parameter LLM.
  Decode step at batch=1: dominant cost = load all weights once, do FP16 matmuls.
  FP16 weights: 7 × 10^9 × 2 B = 14 GB per decode step.
  W4A16 weights: 7 × 10^9 × 0.5 B (INT4 packed) + per-group scales (group_size 128) ≈ 3.5 GB + ~0.11 GB scales.
stem: Based on the memory-traffic estimate above, what is the primary reason W4A16 accelerates batch-1 LLM decode, and by roughly what factor is weight-load traffic reduced?

options.text: Weight-load traffic doubles because per-group scales double the metadata; W4A16 is slower than FP16 for decode.
Weight-load traffic is unchanged because INT4 weights are stored in FP16-sized buffers; the improvement comes purely from INT4 Tensor Core arithmetic.

Weight-load traffic drops by roughly 4× (14 GB → ~3.6 GB including scales); batch-1 decode is dominated by weight loading, so decode throughput improves by close to the same factor, minus overhead from dequantization in registers.
W4A16 accelerates decode by 8× because INT4 uses ¼ the bytes and per-channel scaling gives another 2×.

explanation: INT4 weights use 0.5 bytes/param vs FP16's 2 bytes — a 4× reduction. Per-group scales at group_size 128 add ~1/32 of the FP16 weight size (one FP16 scale per 128 INT4 weights ≈ 0.5 bit per weight in scale metadata), so total is ~3.6 GB vs 14 GB. Batch-1 decode is bandwidth-bound (kernel time is roughly bytes_moved / bandwidth); the observed decode speedup is close to 4× minus dequant-in-register overhead. Option B is false: INT4 is stored packed, not in FP16-sized buffers. Option C is false: scales are small (~1/32 of the weight size), not doubling. Option D fabricates an 8× that has no basis (per-channel scale saves no additional bandwidth in this context).

optionExplanations.C: Correct: 4× traffic reduction + accurate accounting of scales.

assumptions: Batch-1 decode dominated by weight loading.
The dequant kernel achieves close to the theoretical bandwidth (real kernels reach 70-95%).
nonImplications: Does not imply the full 4× speedup is realized in wall-clock — dequant, scale broadcast, and kernel overhead reduce the effective gain to ~2.5-3× in practice.
Does not imply the same argument applies to prefill or large-batch cases — those are compute-bound and W4A16's gain shrinks.

sourceRefs.locator: W4A16 memory traffic vs FP16 analysis

performanceClaim.scope: W4A16 vs FP16 weight-load bandwidth for LLM decode batch-1
